title: 13. Term and Removal of Vice President

blocks.content: The Vice-President holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.

rows: Special Majority (2/3rd total membership) in both Houses
Effective Majority in Rajya Sabha + Simple Majority in Lok Sabha

items: A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can be passed ONLY if 14 days' advance notice has been given.
Unlike the President, no formal impeachment process or constitutional ground is prescribed for removing the Vice-President.
The removal resolution must originate strictly in the Rajya Sabha, not in the Lok Sabha.
The Vice-President continues to hold office beyond his 5-year term until his successor enters upon his office.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Vice-President holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
He can resign from his office at any time by addressing the resignation letter to the President.
A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can be introduced ONLY in the Rajya Sabha.
Removal requires a resolution passed by an effective majority in Rajya Sabha and agreed to by a simple majority in Lok Sabha.
The Constitution does not mention any specific ground for the removal of the Vice-President.
